question_text: A 2-day-old boy fails to pass meconium for the first 48 hours of life. He was born at term to a healthy 19-year-old woman after an uncomplicated pregnancy. At birth, his weight was 3.9 kg (8.6 lb); at the time of presentation, he weighs 3.8 kg (8.4 lb). His vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 70/50 mm Hg, heart rate 130/min, respiratory rate 33/min, and temperature 37.0℃ (98.6℉). On physical examination, he is fussy and appears mildly dehydrated. Bowel sounds are active on auscultation. His abdomen is mildly distended and no masses can be identified on palpation. The patient’s anus is patent. An upper gastrointestinal study with oral contrast demonstrates normal anatomy. A lower gastrointestinal series with barium enema reveals a large amount of retained barium contrast within a dilated sigmoid colon and a normal appearing rectum. The barium solution retention persisted beyond 24 hours after administration. Which of the following best describes the cause of the patient’s symptoms?
